reuse.why: Extends the existing shared getDateWithSkippedWeekend and the RSchedule exdates option rather than writing new move logic; every existing move call site just passes the new list.

duplication.why: The off-day test lives once inside getDateWithSkippedWeekend and the exdate conversion once in getHolidayExdates; only the repeated `exdates: getHolidayExdates(config)` wiring at three RSchedule constructions repeats.

placement.why: Both the move rule and the new exdate helper sit in shared/schedules.ts next to recurConfigToRSchedule, where the tree keeps recurrence rules; call sites only pass data.

scope.why: Focused on the feature (type, shared helper, call sites, tests, release note); the getDatesInRange margin change is a related consequence.

maintainability.why: The daily-skip rule is now split between recurConfigToRSchedule (weekends via byDayOfWeek) and a separate getHolidayExdates that every RSchedule constructor must remember to pass (find-schedules' takeDates does not), so a future caller can silently miss holidays.

bypasses_abstraction.where: All move sites go through getDateWithSkippedWeekend; RSchedule is built through recurConfigToRSchedule as before.

disguised_duplication.where: No duplicated logic; the per-site exdates wiring is repeated call plumbing, not copied logic.

one_place.where: Weekend/holiday moves are decided in one place (getDateWithSkippedWeekend in shared/schedules.ts), but daily skipping is split: weekends in recurConfigToRSchedule, holidays in getHolidayExdates which each RSchedule construction (rule-utils.ts parseRecurDate, schedules/app.ts getUpcomingDates and getDatesInRange) must add itself and find-schedules.ts takeDates does not.
